content:
Hey good people,
I am brand new to doing formalization. I have a preprint out about syntactic approach Ulmer's notion of bialgebras and I've been thinking about formalizing it. Here is the paper:
https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.19587
The point of the paper was to develop minimally 2-algebraic strucures so that I can talk about monoids in monoidal categories or hopf algebras in symmetric monoidal categories and so on, and to prove general properties about these categories. It seems that the syntactic approach works well with Aristotle's autoformalization. It has so far formalized (or it at least claims to) the Induced Functor of Algebras Theorem 3.14 about lifting a (strong) lax functor M\to N to a functor M^T\to N^T between associated (bi)algebras for appropriate (bi)algebraic theories T. I have it currently formalizing some later parts of the paper for me.

I am also able to show how to lift completeness and exactness properties (regularity and exactness) to the categories of bialgebras M^T with suitable assumptions on M and T.

One of the big results of my paper is that as the construction of the category M^T of bialgebras uses only PIE-limits, we have that accessibility of the base M lifts to M^T for all appropriate bialgebraic theories T. This makes me wonder if there people trying to formalize these notions of accessibility and local presentability. If not, I was thinking of trying this out by asking Aristotle to work these things through.

I would really like there to be theory about accessible categories and their PIE-limit closure within the 2-category of categories. There is this recent published paper by Lack and Tendas about accessibility in enriched setting:
arxiv.org/abs/2205.11056
This paper would actually be the one that I'd like to see formalized. It would allow very general monadicity and comonadicity theorems to be formalized for certain enriched categories M^T of bialgebras.

I understand that these kind of autoformalization projects might be annoying to some, but I would appreciate if there were some feedback about how I should approach this project. I was also thinking that maybe the unified approach to bialgebraic structures would be of interest to people who want to have very general definitions.
Have you even tried to use a search engine on the mathlib documentation page?

I did ask from aristotle, but it seems it lied. I now found the library:
https://leanprover-community.github.io/mathlib4_docs/Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Presentable/LocallyPresentable.html
It seems that the base notion is defined. But how would I find if the completeness theorem of Acc of accessible categories, accessible functors and natural transformations is proven, or if there are people working on it? The google's ai seems to say that it is not formalized.

I have formalized the theory of locally presentable categories until the representation theorem #30847, the theory of accessible categories towards the uniformization theorem #31018 and with @Dagur Asgeirsson the fact that accessible functors satisfy the solution set condition #41236. I will also formalize some results about pure subobjects (starting from #41200) as I will need this for homotopical applications.

Nice, good to hear there is interest. The PIE-completeness result would immediately show that for an accessible functor G:D\to C the comma categories c\downarrow G are accessible. The moment when G is continuous and D complete, these comma categories would be complete and hence cocomplete and thus have initial objects. This would show that G is a right adjoint functor. I think accessibility also shows the solution set condition that you want also for the accessible functor G (between accessible categories).

My main interest would be the following two theorems:
1) An accessible category is complete if and only if it is cocomplete.
2) The closure of AccCat under products, inserters and equifiers (PIE-limits) in the 2-category CAT of categories. This could also be generalized to the enriched setting (w.r.t. flexible 2-limits) via the paper by Lack and Tendas, where the base of enrichment is a locally presentable symmetric monoidal closed category. This would be cool to see formalized but it is difficult.

The \lambda-pure subobjects form an important route through which Rocisky and Adamek pass. I should check more carefully how much do Lack and Tendas rely on these older results.

I had a rough project to show that categories of algebras for an accessible monad on a locally presentable category is presentable. My intention was to intentionally avoid the Adamek-Rosicky approach that also uses PIE-limits (because that would open the can of worms of formalizing these notion) and to instead try to follow a paper by Kelly, but this project is currently not moving.

The harmonic's formalization ai-bot Aristotle now claims that it has formally verified most of my paper except for the part talking about accessibility. Would it be okay to ask it to try to formalize theory related to accessibility? I am also unsure what to do with these claimed formalizations. I'll ask some AI's if they even make sense. At least the bot agrees with the results, which is of course nice to hear.

I set the bot to formalize the PIE limit closure of Acc. Let's see what comes out of it. It's very good that there is already prior work been done in this direction so it doesn't create the definitions by itself. I doubt that the bot is able to do it by itself but who knows.

The bot claims to have formalized the PIE-completeness of the 2-category Acc of accessible categories.

It includes the proof of Makkai-Pare uniformization theorem.

It claims to have followed Locally Presentable and Accessible categories-book.

As corollaries the bot claims to have formalized the adjoint functor theorems for accessible functors, characterization of locally presentable categories as accessible embedded reflective subcategories of pre-sheaf categories.
I'll play around a bit more with the bot but at some point it would be perhaps useful for someone else to judge the code the bot has produced.

You should have your bot look at open mathlib PRs (particularly the ones mentioned by Joël above) to avoid redoing material that will soon be in mathlib. Then, instead of asking humans to read all the AI-generated code, have your bot make a comparator setup (it will figure out what this means). Then humans will only need to read the sorried statements in the challenge file, and check that they correspond to the informal statements you want to formalize
okay, I'll try to figure this out, thanks!
